9v batteries run longer than, say, a button battery. They can work for months with normal on/off use. This schematic also has a switch.

  • Use any latching on/off switch. Not all switches stay on, some are just momentary switches which are on only while you hold down the switch.
  • Use the dimmer to dim the light to save even more power. This dimmer is a "thumb wheel potentiometer" but other potentiometers can be used. This is a 10k knob pot. A 10k value means it has, at most, a resistance of 10,000 ohms. This should be enough to turn the light off, or close to it. But just in case I added a switch.
  • Notice how the 9v + terminal reaches the + terminal of the LED. LEDs are Light Emitting Diodes. As a diode it only allows electricity to flow one way. If you wire the LED backwards it won't hurt it, it just won't light. I normally mark the - leg with a black marker. In the US, black wires stand for negative/ground/common, and red wires stand for positive/hot.
  • If you accidentally wire in a resistor with a lower value (lower resistance) the LED will pop, and you just bury it with a quick ceremony. That's why I get bags of 10 LEDs at once. Plus, parts are much cheaper in lots of 10 or 20.
  • This version does not use a joule thief. But it will still work well.
Simple DIY LED light with 9v battery
